headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0056 — The window SMTO was about to use has changed or closed

html:
SMTO-EXE-0056 — The window SMTO was about to use has changed or closed

GUID: 8e740f17-d52f-57fc-9c29-24ad2ce33e7e
Slug: desktop-stale-window
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: desktop

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to act on a window it had seen earlier, but that window has closed, changed, or was seen before the Gateway restarted. SMTO stopped instead of guessing which window you meant.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the window you want is still open on the Gateway computer. If it was closed, there is nothing for SMTO to act on.
  2. Ask SMTO to list the open windows again (for example "show me the open windows"), then tell it which one you mean. Window references expire when a window closes or the Gateway restarts, so SMTO needs a fresh look.
  3. Before asking for the action again, look at the window to see whether your earlier request already took effect. The window may have changed just as the earlier request arrived.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finds the window in a fresh list and the requested action completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer. Don't tell SMTO to act on any matching window as a workaround; it should act only on the one you chose.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Desktop window identity could not be decoded (e.g. issued before a Gateway restart) or matched to a current window, the application had no window, or the native API reported the target as invalid.

What this means

  • An opaque window identity could not be decoded or matched to a current window, no application window existed, or the native API classified the target as stale. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • An opaque window identity could not be decoded or matched to a current window, no application window existed, or the native API classified the target as stale.

How to diagnose it

  • Refresh window metadata on the same Gateway and compare exact identity, application and current state.

How to fix it

  • Call desktop.windows again on the same Gateway and select the current exact window_id; identities are signed per Gateway process lifetime and become invalid after a restart. For macOS AX -25202 failures the receipt may mark effect_unknown, so observe the window's state before sending a new action.
  • List windows again and deliberately select the current exact window before requesting a new action.

Retry and execution caution

  • List windows again and deliberately select the current exact window before requesting a new action.

How to verify the fix

  • The deliberately selected current window resolves before another action is sent.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass identity protection or automatically replay an uncertain mutation.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
